waypoints.name: Upper South Fork Skokomish Trailhead (Trail #873)
waypoints.note: Reached via Skokomish Valley Rd / FS-23 / FS-2361 from Shelton; FS-2361 gated Oct 1-Apr 30. Standard route follows Trail 873 to Sundown Lake, then east along the Six Ridge crest past McGravey Lakes and Belview Camp to the overgrown 'Mount Olson Way' spur.
waypoints.directions: From US 101 north of Shelton, turn west on West Skokomish Valley Road, follow it about 5.6 miles and continue uphill onto Forest Road 23. Stay on FS 23, keeping left at intersections, then turn right onto FS 2361 and drive about 5 miles to the road end at about 1,100 ft. FS 2361 is rough and potholed and is closed to vehicles October 1 to April 30.

waypoints.name: South Fork Skokomish River ford
waypoints.note: Unbridged ford of the Skokomish's south bank; safely crossable (ankle-deep) only in late summer/early fall low water, otherwise a serious hazard.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Upper South Fork Skokomish Trail #873 up the valley on brushy but obvious tread, crossing Rule Creek on a bridge, to the unbridged ford of the South Fork at about 2.4 miles. It is ankle-deep only in late-summer low water.

waypoints.name: Olympic National Park boundary
waypoints.note: Trail leaves Olympic National Forest and enters Olympic National Park/Wilderness; a wilderness camping permit, reserved in advance, is required for overnight stays beyond this point, tread grows fainter above here.
waypoints.directions: Continue up the valley on the far bank to the Olympic National Park boundary near 5.1 miles, where the trail begins to climb steeply and the tread grows fainter.

waypoints.name: Sundown Pass
waypoints.note: Forested saddle marked by a broken signpost, reached via steep, faint tread through wet subalpine meadows; junction with the Six Ridge Trail heading east along the crest toward Mount Olson.
waypoints.directions: Climb steeply on faint, broken tread through wet subalpine meadows to the forested saddle of Sundown Pass at about 4,125 ft, marked by a broken signpost.

waypoints.name: Lake Sundown
waypoints.note: Short spur off the pass to a subalpine basin lake on Six Ridge's western flank; a designated camp, with more water further east at McGravey Lakes and a spring at Belview Camp.
waypoints.directions: From the pass, continue about 0.4 mile to Lake Sundown, a designated camp in a subalpine basin.

waypoints.name: Six Ridge crest / Mount Olson boot-path junction
waypoints.note: Point on Six Ridge's sawtooth crest closest to Olson where an unsigned, unofficial boot path ('Mount Olson Way') leaves the trail for the peak; faint and overgrown with blowdowns and lingering snowfields into midsummer.
waypoints.directions: Climb steeply from the lake to Six Ridge Pass, then follow the primitive Six Ridge Trail east along the sawtooth crest past McGravey Lakes and Belview Camp to about 4,650 ft, the point on the crest nearest Olson, where the unsigned Mount Olson Way leaves the trail.

waypoints.name: Tarn below Olson's summit block
waypoints.note: Boulder-field tarn just below the summit block is the last water and a common bivy spot; the final gully above it to the top is steep, loose, and exposed.
waypoints.directions: Follow the faint, overgrown Mount Olson Way on a steep sidehill traverse, crossing a loose notch and dropping into the basin to the boulder-field tarn below the summit block.

waypoints.name: Mount Olson
waypoints.directions: Climb to the pass immediately east of the summit, then scramble the steep Class 3 grass and heather slope above it, around 55-60 degrees in places. It eases and curves around the north side of the peak onto a heather bench, then it is an easy walk to the true summit.

approach_variants.name: South Fork Skokomish Trail #873 to Sundown Pass, then the Six Ridge crest and the Mount Olson Way
approach_variants.notes:
Mount Olson sees very few ascents and is normally reached as a side trip off the long Six Ridge traverse. From the Upper South Fork Skokomish Trailhead (Trail #873), reached via Skokomish Valley Road, FS-23 and FS-2361 from Shelton — FS-2361 is gated 1 October to 30 April — the trail runs up the valley. There is an unbridged ford of the South Fork at about 2.4 miles and 1,450 ft that is only ankle-deep and safely crossable in late summer or early autumn low water; at other times it is a serious hazard. The Olympic National Park boundary comes near 5.1 miles, after which tread grows fainter and an advance-reserved wilderness permit is required for overnight stays.

Sundown Pass, a forested saddle marked by a broken signpost, comes at about 7.2 miles and 4,125 ft — this is the junction with the Six Ridge Trail heading east along the crest. Lake Sundown is a short spur off the pass at about 7.6 miles and 3,810 ft and is a designated camp; small streams toward McGravey Lakes and a spring at Belview Camp further along the ridge also supply water.

Follow the Six Ridge Trail east along its sawtooth crest — a ridge either side with a gully in the middle, and brutal uphill for every downhill — past McGravey Lakes and Belview Camp to about 4,650 ft, where an unsigned, unofficial boot path known as the Mount Olson way leaves the trail for the peak. It is faint and overgrown with blowdown and lingering snowfields into midsummer. A boulder-field tarn at about 5,100 ft below the summit block is the last water and a common bivy.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jul-Sep, and gated by two fords that are only reliably safe in late summer and early autumn low water
hazards: Two unbridged fords only safely crossable in late summer and early autumn low water
Route-finding on trail-less and boot-path terrain with an unsigned departure from Six Ridge
Dense brush and blowdown along the Six Ridge approach
A 55-60 degree grass and heather summit pitch that is loose and exposed, and worse descending
FS-2361 is gated 1 October to 30 April
Afternoon weather on an exposed crest, and a multi-day return from a very lightly visited peak
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The base of the climb is the pass immediately east of the summit, and the test is that the climbing starts the moment you stand in it. From the pass, the final ascent to Olson's 5,289 ft top is a steep, unmarked scramble up a grassy and heather slope pitched around 55-60 degrees in places — hands-on, solid Class 3 — directly above you. Grass and heather at that angle is a distinctive surface: it is neither talus nor rock, and you are either on it or you are not.

Second test, and it is what tells you the slope is easing correctly rather than that you have wandered: the pitch eases and curves round the north side of the peak onto a heather bench, and then it is an easy stroll to the true summit. So the sequence is steep grass, then a bench that takes you leftward round the peak, then a walk. If the ground stays steep all the way to a top, or if you are on rock and scree rather than heather, you are on the wrong side.

The approach test before any of that is the departure from Six Ridge, because it is the thing people miss: the Mount Olson Way leaves the Six Ridge Trail at the point on the sawtooth crest closest to Olson, at about 4,650 ft, and it is unsigned. It is faint, overgrown and blowdown-choked. If you are still on obvious trail after passing the point where the crest is nearest the peak, you have walked past the turn.

Honest limit: there is no documented roped climbing route, rack or pitch-by-pitch description for this peak. It is recorded as a summit without a route write-up. This is a bushwhack and scramble objective for peak-baggers, and the markers above are the sum of what has been written down. Treat the notch and the upper summit meadow as the crux going both ways: both are loose and exposed and better handled with an axe or a pole for self-arrest, especially wet or under late snow.

itinerary.cal: FR 2361 to the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead is closed to vehicles Oct 1-Apr 30; the trail beyond Sundown Lake is essentially unmaintained (heavy blowdown, faint tread, easy to lose) and dry beyond Camp Bellevue, so this is best done July-September after snow/blowdown clears, carrying/caching all water for the final push.

days.note: From the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead, climb the South Fork Skokomish River Trail over Sundown Pass to Sundown Lake, then pick up the primitive, largely unmaintained Six Ridge Trail over Six Ridge Pass to McGravey Lakes. Parties describe near-constant route-finding through overgrown meadows, faded cairns, and repeated ridge undulations; camp near McGravey Lakes or Camp Bellevue, the last reliable water before the peak.
days.title: Approach to high camp near McGravey Lakes / Camp Bellevue
days.objective: Reach a high camp below Mount Olson via Sundown Pass and the primitive Six Ridge Trail

days.note: From camp, sidehill the faint Mount Olson Way Trail across broken, exposed ground to a small tarn at the base of the peak, then scramble roughly 1,000 ft up steep meadow and heather (55-60 degrees in spots, hands-on rock, rated class 3 in the published description) to the summit block. Descend the same way back to camp.
days.title: Summit push via the Mount Olson Way Trail and boot path

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Start along the faint Mount Olson Way Trail toward the peak.

schedule.label: Reach the tarn below Mount Olson
schedule.detail: Steep, faint side-hill traverse over a ridge/saddle to the small tarn at the peak's base.

schedule.label: Start the boot path
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scramble up steep meadow and heather on the SE-facing slope.

schedule.label: Summit (5,289 ft)
schedule.detail: Curve around a heather bench near the top to the true summit; views across the interior Olympics.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the boot path and ridge back down to the tarn.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the Mount Olson Way Trail traverse to camp.

days.objective: Climb Mount Olson (5,289 ft) via the tarn and SE-face boot path

days.note: Reverse the Six Ridge / Sundown Pass approach back to the car. It's mostly net downhill, but the primitive tread, brush, and repeated ridge undulations still make it a full day.
days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A rugged ~3-day, ~19-mile round trip via Sundown Pass and the primitive Six Ridge/Mount Olson Way Trail, with a high camp near McGravey Lakes/Camp Bellevue and a steep class 2-3 scramble to the 5,289 ft summit — not a car-to-car day trip.
